title: Closed Monoidal Categories and the Internal Hom

items.title: Left-closed, right-closed, and biclosed monoidal categories
The internal hom is unique up to unique natural isomorphism
items.strategy: Fix the tensor parameter and apply uniqueness of right adjoints to the corresponding tensor functor; naturality in the remaining variable is inherited from the adjoint-uniqueness theorem.

items.title: The internal hom and its evaluation morphism
A supplied symmetry identifies the left and right internal homs
items.strategy: Transport the right-closure adjunction across the given natural isomorphism X tensor A ~= A tensor X, then invoke uniqueness of right adjoints.

items.title: A monoidal category need not be closed
items.strategy: Use the five-element diamond lattice as a poset-category under meet. The induced strict monoidal structure exists, but for one atom p and a different atom q the set of x with p wedge x <= q has no greatest element, so p wedge - has no right adjoint.

items.title: In a biclosed monoidal category tensor is cocontinuous in each variable
items.strategy: Each tensor-with-a-fixed-object functor is a left adjoint when the corresponding closure exists, so the published left-adjoint preservation theorem applies on each side.

items.title: The internal hom preserves limits in the covariant variable and sends colimits to limits in the contravariant variable
items.strategy: Apply the right-adjoint preservation theorem to each closure. For the contravariant variable, pass to the opposite category so that left closure becomes an ordinary right-adjoint statement.

items.title: The internal-hom composition morphism
items.strategy: Transpose the composite [Y,Z] tensor [X,Y] tensor X -> [Y,Z] tensor Y -> Z to obtain composition, define the unit by transposing the unitor X ~= 1 tensor X, and prove associativity and unit laws by uniqueness of transposes.

items.title: The tensor unit is an internal-hom unit
items.strategy: Because tensoring with the unit is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor, compare its right adjoint with the identity and then evaluate the transposition bijection at the tensor unit.

items.title: Exponential object
Cartesian closed category
Set is cartesian closed
items.strategy: Use the ordinary finite products in Set and identify function sets as exponentials via the published currying adjunction.

items.title: The category of small categories is cartesian closed
items.strategy: Use Cat's cartesian monoidal structure and show that functors C x D -> E curry naturally to functors C -> [D,E].

items.title: A presheaf category on a small category is cartesian closed
items.strategy: For presheaves P and Q define Q^P(c) as Nat(y(c) x P, Q), define restriction by precomposition, and use Yoneda plus Set-currying to prove Nat(H x P, Q) ~= Nat(H, Q^P).

items.title: Currying and uncurrying are mutually inverse
items.strategy: Iterate the basic transposition bijection in a cartesian closed category, use associativity of products to compare bracketings, and use the internal-hom composition map to identify repeated currying operations.

items.title: In a cartesian closed category, any initial object is strict
items.strategy: Because product with a fixed object is a left adjoint, it preserves the initial object. The resulting A x 0 ~= 0 identity makes every map into 0 invertible.

items.title: A cartesian closed preorder has relative implications
items.strategy: Translate the exponential adjunction in a thin category into order language, using that products in a poset-category are meets.

items.title: Slice categories, composition, and pullback along a morphism
Locally cartesian closed category
Slices of a locally cartesian closed category are locally cartesian closed
items.strategy: Identify a slice of a slice, (C/X)/a, with C/A and transport cartesian closedness across that isomorphism.

items.title: A locally cartesian closed category with a terminal object is cartesian closed
items.strategy: Use the canonical equivalence C ~= C/1 for a terminal object 1.

items.title: A locally cartesian closed category has pullbacks, and with a terminal object it has all finite limits
items.strategy: Realize pullbacks as binary products in slice categories, then add the terminal object to recover all finite limits.

items.title: Local cartesian closure is equivalent to every pullback functor having a right adjoint
items.strategy: One direction uses the cartesian closed structure in each slice to define dependent products Pi_f; the converse applies the hypothesis inside each slice, whose terminal object is the identity morphism.

items.title: Set is locally cartesian closed
items.strategy: For a function f : X -> Y, define the right adjoint Pi_f on a family over X by its fiberwise function sets over each y in Y and verify the resulting pullback adjunction.

items.title: Subobject classifier
With a supplied well-powering, a subobject classifier represents the subobject functor
items.strategy: Use pullback of truth along a map X -> Omega to define a subobject of X, then use the uniqueness clause in the classifier definition to show this is inverse to the characteristic-map construction on the supplied representative sets.

items.title: The two-element set is a subobject classifier for Set
items.strategy: Identify monomorphisms in Set with subset inclusions and send each subset to its characteristic function into {0,1}.

items.title: Boundary: this page stops before elementary and Grothendieck toposes
FALSE: every monoidal category is closed
items.strategy: Refute the claim with the diamond-lattice monoidal category from cex-a-monoidal-category-need-not-be-closed.

items.title: FALSE: the left and right internal homs agree in every monoidal category
items.strategy: Refute the claim with a non-symmetric bimodule-tensor example, where the two closures are different Hom-bimodules.

items.title: FALSE: every cartesian closed category has all finite limits
items.strategy: Use the cartesian closed category of nonempty sets, where the equalizer of two maps may be empty and therefore need not exist.

items.title: FALSE: every cartesian closed category is locally cartesian closed
items.strategy: Use the cartesian closed category of nonempty sets and show that the slice over a two-point set lacks the product of the two singleton inclusions.

items.title: FALSE: a subobject classifier is any object representing monomorphisms
items.strategy: Compare the classifier definition with a pair of distinct monomorphisms representing the same subobject; representing monomorphisms themselves forgets the uniqueness-up-to-subobject-class needed by item 25.

title: Closed Monoidal Categories and the Internal Hom - Examples

items.title: A function set computed as an exponential object
items.strategy: Pick small finite sets, write the evaluation map explicitly, and check the currying bijection on every function by hand.

items.title: Currying for sets of three variables
items.strategy: Start from a concrete map A x B x C -> D, curry it in two stages, and verify that uncurrying in either order recovers the original map.

items.title: The internal hom of abelian groups
items.strategy: View Ab as Z-Mod, identify the internal hom with Hom_Z(B,C), and compute the evaluation morphism and its transpose on explicit generators.

items.title: The exponential of two small categories computed on a walking-arrow source
items.strategy: Take the walking-arrow category as the exponent, identify functors into a target with its arrows, and write the induced currying bijection explicitly.

items.title: A slice of Set computed as a locally cartesian closed category
items.strategy: Choose a small map f : X -> Y, compute pullback along f and the corresponding dependent product Pi_f on finite fibers, and check one adjunction instance directly.

items.title: The subobject classifier in a presheaf category on the walking arrow
items.strategy: For a tiny source category, compute the subobjects of the representables, package them into the classifier presheaf, and classify a concrete subpresheaf by pullback.
